artists.biography: Ride were a British shoegazing band that formed in 1988 in Oxford, England, consisting of Andy Bell, Mark Gardener, Laurence "Loz" Colbert, and Steve Queralt. The band were initially part of the "shoegazing" scene that emerged in England during the early 1990s. Following the break-up of the band in 1996, members moved on to various other projects, most notably Bell who became the bassist for Oasis. In 2001, the band members were briefly reunited for a one-off performance for a television show. Their debut album 'Nowhere' has been named one of the greatest albums of the shoegazing genre, Nowhere was voted number 74 on Pitchfork Media's list of the Top 100 Albums of the 1990s, and closing track "Vapour Trail" was voted at number 145 on Pitchfork's Top 200 Tracks of the 90s. The album is also included in the book '1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die'.

perplexity.description:
Carnival of Light is the third studio album by British rock band Ride, originally released in June 1994 via Creation Records. Musically, the album marks a departure from the band's earlier shoegaze and dream pop roots, embracing a broader sonic palette that incorporates elements of Britpop, psychedelic rock, and classic British guitar traditions. Produced by John Leckie and featuring contributions from future Radiohead producer Nigel Godrich (except for one track produced by George Drakoulias), the album is notable for its split songwriting approach: Andy Bell's tracks dominate the second half, while Mark Gardener's songs open the record. Guest appearances include Jon Lord of Deep Purple on keyboards, adding a distinctive classic rock flavor.

Within Ride's discography, Carnival of Light stands as a transitional work, bridging their early, effects-laden sound with a more song-oriented, accessible style. Released at the height of the Britpop era, the album arrived when the music press was increasingly focused on bands like Oasis and Blur, making Ride's more expansive and psychedelic approach somewhat out of step with prevailing trends. While it reached number 5 on the UK Albums Chart, the album received mixed critical reactions upon release, with some praising its ambition and others finding it less cohesive than their earlier work. Despite this, Carnival of Light remains a significant entry in Ride's catalog, reflecting their willingness to evolve and experiment during a pivotal moment in British rock.
